records: {MACRO:FA}, His Majesty is waiting for you.
Preserve the surname macro and formal royal summons; add no personal title.
Ah, {MACRO:FA}! Splendid work! Our nation's prosperity is assured!
The king celebrates Hodram's achievement in an expansive royal voice.
I appoint you supreme commander of the navy. I look forward to still greater achievements as you build on its strength.
Preserve the explicit new naval appointment and expectation of continued service.
Retain Gerhard's impressed aside, not a spoken interruption.
Charles privately considers the appointment an ideal fit.
Hodram pauses over the offered office before requesting retirement.
And you may name your reward. Is there anything you desire?
Preserve the king's open-ended offer without inventing a reward menu.
Keep Hodram's hesitation before the consequential request.
May I speak freely of what I wish, Your Majesty?
Use respectful, natural court speech for the request to state his wish.
The king explicitly permits an unrestricted answer.
Preserve the pause as Hodram commits to his request.
I am deeply honored by your offer to appoint me supreme commander. However...
Retain gratitude for the appointment before the refusal; do not make him accept it.
The king notices the unexpected qualification.
If you would permit such selfishness... I would like to retire from the navy.
Keep the explicit retirement request and deferential delivery.
Charles's private, drawn-out astonishment contrasts with the formal audience.
Gerhard's shocked aside remains separate from Charles's reaction.
What is the meaning of this!?
The king demands an explanation rather than granting retirement immediately.
It is something I have considered for some time.
Establish that Hodram's decision predates this audience.
The king listens in silence before Hodram explains further.
I was fortunate to have exceptional people under my command. With their help, I have managed to accomplish the great task of building the world's strongest navy.
Preserve gratitude to his subordinates and qualified success, without inventing a different military objective.
Your Majesty placed your trust in me despite my shortcomings. Your kindness made this possible, and I am deeply grateful. However...
Localize the formal self-effacement naturally while preserving his thanks and impending reservation.
I lack the talent to maintain that strength, guide the many recruits yet to come through military discipline, and make the royal navy an enduring institution.
Retain all three leadership concerns; this is Hodram's stated limitation, not proof of actual incompetence.
Nonsense. The mere fact that you lead our navy strikes fear into other nations and inspires our men!
The king argues for the deterrent and morale value of Hodram's presence.
Forgive me for contradicting you, Your Majesty, but that is precisely what concerns me most.
Hodram respectfully challenges the king's proposed advantage.
The king requests clarification of the unexpected objection.

With respect, if we needlessly put our enemies on guard, we will eventually find ourselves isolated. If our own forces grow arrogant in the belief that they are the world's strongest, disaster will surely follow.
Preserve foreign isolation and domestic overconfidence as distinct strategic dangers.
My absence would let other nations lower their guard, while keeping our own officers and men alert to danger.
Keep both sides of the argument for his departure, including foreign complacency rather than new hostility.
The king considers the argument without agreeing yet.
I ask for nothing else. I beg Your Majesty's indulgence in granting this selfish wish.
Retirement is his sole requested reward; preserve the final respectful appeal.
Retain the king's pause before the reluctant decision.
Very well... I deeply regret it, but if this is truly your wish, I have little choice.
The king reluctantly accepts; do not turn the departure into dismissal or punishment.
I am most grateful, Your Majesty.
Render the formal expression of gratitude without copying ceremonial Japanese syntax.
Manuel's silence is its own reaction to the accepted retirement.
Keep Charles's subdued private address after the audience's emotional turn.
Retain Gerhard's separate silence before the farewell scene.
{MACRO:FI}... Won't you come to my country?
Sera asks him to accompany her; preserve the name macro and personal appeal.
Ah... It seems the sea is the only place I can really live.
Hodram's refusal reflects his attachment to seafaring, not hostility to Sera's homeland.
And this may sound cold, but rebuilding your homeland is something you and your people must accomplish yourselves.
Keep the difficult insistence on her people's agency without promising to rebuild the country for them.
But I... I want you to come, {MACRO:FI}.
Sera repeats her personal wish hesitantly; cinematic staging remains unformatted.
Preserve the explicit denial of a legendary identity, not a newly invented royal comparison.
Sera tries to persist but cannot finish her thought; do not complete it with a proposal or confession.
Keep Hodram's silent response; source right-side placement needs separate native qualification.
You're a princess. I'm just a retired officer now. Our stations are worlds apart.
Both princess status and retirement are explicit here; do not add marriage, betrothal or a legal prohibition.
Retain Sera's silence after the difference in their positions is stated.
Don't look so sad. This isn't goodbye forever.
Hodram softens the farewell and makes room for later visits.
Retain the explicit Sera heading and tentative question; structural heading placement awaits cinematic geometry.
Preserve the captain-name macro in the explicit heading, not an added spoken self-introduction.
Retain the explicit Sera heading and silent emotional beat.
{MACRO:FI}: I mean it. I'm a free man now.
Hodram reassures her using his new freedom after retirement; preserve the heading macro.
{MACRO:FI}: I'll visit from time to time and see how your country is coming back to life.
The promise is periodic visits to witness rebuilding, not permanent residence or engagement.
Sera quietly accepts the reassurance; retain the explicit heading.
Sirwood, take care of Sera for me.
Use the established Sirwood name and request care without inventing a familial or romantic relationship.
Sirwood's halting newly learned language intentionally omits a pronoun; do not make it fluent yet.
Oh? Has Sera been teaching you? I look forward to hearing you next time we meet.
Hodram infers language lessons and anticipates progress; keep the question as an inference.
Sera calls after him, preserving the name macro and emotional hesitation.
Hodram's silent response belongs to the right-side source staging; layout is still pending.
Keep Sera's urgent request for a visit, not a demand for permanent return.
Retain Sera's quiet beat before Hodram addresses her again.
Keep the gentle direct address without adding a relationship label.
It won't be easy, but take care of yourself.
Preserve the difficult work ahead and caring farewell; do not promise to undertake it himself.
Keep Sera's nonverbal assent rather than inventing spoken dialogue.
Retain both the reassurance of reunion and actual parting.
Now then... Where should I go?
Hodram considers his destination after leaving Sera; no new route is chosen yet.
Admiral! We're ready to sail whenever you are!
Gerhard's familiar call interrupts the solitary departure; keep the source address despite retirement.
Retain Hodram's surprise at finding him there.
Gerhard cheerfully resumes their established command dynamic.
Gerhard! What are you doing here!?
Hodram questions Gerhard's presence, setting up a deliberately literal reply.
Well, I've been finding you a new ship, stocking her, and making all the preparations to sail...
Preserve all three concrete preparations and Gerhard's evasive literal answer.
That's not what I mean. I had positions of responsibility arranged for everyone under my command.
Hodram had posts arranged for the whole group; do not restrict them to named male companions.
Yes, Charles is now director of the Royal Academy's research institute. He's delighted to have all the research equipment he could possibly want.
Preserve the precise institute role and Charles's enthusiasm; do not make him head of the entire academy.
Keep Hodram's interrupted attempt to bring the conversation back to Gerhard.
Of course, of course. Manuel is chairman of the maritime technology committee. Last I saw, he was studying plans for a new ship, looking unusually solemn.
Keep Manuel's actual committee office, ship-design work and humorous change in demeanor.
No! You were entrusted with the responsibility of supreme commander of the navy!
The new office assigned to Gerhard is explicit; do not invent a lower rank or treat him as still unappointed.
It's not for me... You'll have to excuse me.
Gerhard declines the role modestly rather than asserting he was rejected.
Don't be ridiculous. I chose you for your ability, your experience, and the respect you command.
Retain all three reasons for Hodram's selection of Gerhard.
Admiral, isn't it rather unfair to leave me with all that responsibility while you enjoy a comfortable retirement?
Gerhard gently turns Hodram's own retirement against him; keep the affectionate complaint.
Hodram is caught off guard by the fair accusation.
A country's defense should be the responsibility of its own people. An outsider like me has no business interfering.
Keep Gerhard's outsider argument as his own stated reason; add no nationality or citizenship history.
Besides, without you here, I have no reason to stay in this country. I'll follow you wherever you go.
Preserve his personal loyalty and decision to accompany Hodram without inventing kinship or romance.
Allow Hodram's silent response before the closing joke.
Not much prospect of romance on this voyage, then.
Retain the wry reference to a voyage without feminine company, setting up Gerhard's reply.
Ha ha ha! Whatever do you mean? Two handsome fellows like us? The ladies won't leave us alone wherever we go!
Preserve Gerhard's warm, self-confident humor and the joke about both men, not a hostile insult.
Hodram's dry closing aside answers Gerhard affectionately; cinematic placement remains pending.
